kn.dserver.armBuild: ARM servers (Ampere, Raspberry Pi) have no ready-made package yet: build it from source (a few minutes) and run it from the source folder, which has the maps.
kn.dserver.cfg.bots: Keep N bots in the lobby, or fill it up to N players with bots that leave as people join.
kn.dserver.cfg.hostname: The server's name in the server browser.
kn.dserver.cfg.online: {2}1{3}: signed-in players are checked with the account service, so names cannot be faked. Guests still join.
kn.dserver.cfg.password: Players need it to join; {2}""{3} = open.
kn.dserver.cfg.publicIp: The address players connect to: your public IP or a domain. Leave it unset only for LAN games.
kn.dserver.cfg.rcon: With {2}rcon_port{3}: a remote console on 127.0.0.1 ({2}server_bin --rcon{3}). Never forward it.
kn.dserver.cfg.region: Region code shown in the list.
kn.dserver.cfgIntro: One {2}key value{3} per line, {2}//{3} comments, quotes around values with spaces. Flags on the command line win over the file.
kn.dserver.cgnat: If the router's WAN address is not your public IP, your provider shares one address between customers (CGNAT) and forwarding cannot work: ask them for a public IPv4, or use a VPS.
kn.dserver.console: The window it runs in is its console: {2}status{3}, {2}players{3}, {2}kick{3}, {2}map{3}, {2}say{3}, {2}help{3}. Ctrl+C lets the round finish, then stops it. To upgrade, copy only the new {2}server_bin{3} over: {2}cfg/server.cfg{3} is yours.
kn.dserver.desc: Run your own Krunker Box Office server on your computer or a VPS. Players find it in the server browser or join it by address.
kn.dserver.howLinux: Unpack it, edit {2}cfg/server.cfg{3} and run {2}./server_bin{3}. It needs libcurl and OpenSSL: {2}sudo apt install libcurl4 libssl3 libcrypt1{3}.
kn.dserver.howMac: Unpack it, edit {2}cfg/server.cfg{3} and run {2}./server_bin{3} in Terminal. It is not notarized: the first time, run {2}xattr -d com.apple.quarantine server_bin *.dylib{3} in its folder.
kn.dserver.howWindows: Unzip it anywhere, edit {2}cfg\server.cfg{3} and run {0}server_bin.exe{1}. Allow it when Windows Firewall asks (private and public networks).
kn.dserver.latest: Rolling build {2}server-latest{3}: it matches the current game. Servers on an older build show as Outdated in the server browser.
kn.dserver.list2: The coordinator then asks the server for its info over UDP
kn.dserver.list3: Optional: {2}online_mode 1{3} checks signed-in players with the account service (coordinator.krunk.io), so their names and accounts are real. Guests can still play.
kn.dserver.network: Running servers for a community network with its own coordinator? Its operator gives you {2}coordinator_url{3} and {2}coordinator_secret{3}: that links the server to their accounts, skins and matchmaking. Without them the server runs standalone.
kn.dserver.noPackage: No ready-made server for this computer
kn.dserver.noPackageSub: Build it from source (below, Linux on ARM), or run it on a Linux x86_64 server
kn.dserver.pkg.linux-x86_64: Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+ (OpenSSL 3): the one for a VPS
kn.dserver.pkg.windows-x86_64: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit: the DLLs it needs are in the zip
kn.dserver.ports1: Give the computer a fixed local address: a DHCP reservation in the router (e.g. {2}192.168.1.50{3}).
kn.dserver.ports2: Open the router's page (usually {2}192.168.0.1{3} or {2}192.168.1.1{3}), find Port Forwarding (also called NAT, Virtual Server or Applications) and add {2}
kn.dserver.ports3: Let it through the computer's firewall: allow server_bin when Windows asks, or {2}sudo ufw allow
kn.dserver.ports4: Set {2}public_ip{3} to your public address (a "what is my IP" site shows it) and test from another network: {2}python3 kn-query.py your-ip
kn.dserver.portsIntro: Players outside your home network reach the server only through port {0}
kn.dserver.quick1: Download your platform's package above and unpack it anywhere.
kn.dserver.quick2: Open {2}cfg/server.cfg{3} and set at least {2}hostname{3} and, on a public server, {2}public_ip{3} (the address players connect to). Every key is explained in {2}server.cfg.example{3}.
kn.dserver.quick3: Run {2}./server_bin{3} in that folder ({2}server_bin.exe{3} on Windows). Or paste the command from Host Game's last step: it carries the map, mode and rules you picked.
kn.dserver.recommended: RECOMMENDED: A LINUX SERVER OR VPS
kn.dserver.title: Dedicated Server
kn.dserver.vps.note: Approximate prices as of October 2026 (checked 2026-10-15), before VAT, for the smallest plan; providers change them often and some plans sell out. Check the provider's page before you buy. Krunker Box Office is not affiliated with any of them.
kn.dserver.vpsIntro: A small rented Linux server keeps a lobby up around the clock without touching your home network. One {2}server_bin{3} is one lobby and needs little: about 110 MB of memory and a few percent of one CPU with a full lobby, so the cheapest plan is enough. Pick a location close to your players.
